sources.cite: CDC, About the National Syndromic Surveillance Program (NSSP)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch: facilities send de-identified records with chief complaint, diagnosis codes, patient characteristics and location; 'Within 24 hours of a patient's ED visit, data are available in NSSP for analysis'; '85% of U.S. emergency departments send data to NSSP'; health departments use it to 'detect unusual levels of illness to determine whether a response is needed' and to 'monitor disease trends'.

sources.cite: Virginia Department of Health, Limitations of Syndromic Surveillance Data
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch: the chief complaint is a near real-time field 'commonly recorded as a free text field, which may include misspellings or abbreviations'; diagnosis transmission 'can be delayed'; changes in the number of reporting facilities 'should be taken into consideration when interpreting trends'. The page did not discuss feed outages; that a stopped or changed feed must be found before trends are read is the author's application of its point about participation.

brief.situation: You are the informatics analyst at Cedar County Public Health (fictional). Four emergency departments send syndromic data: each visit's chief complaint and diagnosis codes, de-identified, within a day. This week the share of ED visits that look like influenza-like illness (ILI) fell from 6.1% to 3.4%. Two of the hospitals moved to a new EHR on Monday. The weekly report goes to hospitals and the public at 12:00. It is 10:45.
handover: ILI is flagged from the chief complaint text (fever with cough or sore throat).
Each facility's informatics contact is on the feed roster.
howItWorks: Pick a step from the action list: check completeness or fields, change how the share is computed, run a check, or send the report. Nothing you pick is typed or executed: every step shows an authored result.
Each step takes working minutes, and the clock moves by the minutes it takes. The deadline runs on the same clock.
Sending the report is final for this case. Afterwards you record what you found and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The report goes out at 12:00, 75 minutes after the start; invented.

writeup.question: For the epidemiologist: why the ILI share fell, what you reported, and how you know it is right.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: A data feed problem, not epidemiology: Riverside's feed stopped (completeness) and Northgate's chief complaints arrive empty (a field mapping change), both after EHR go-lives on Monday; the share's facility set changed.
parts.modelAnswer: Two EHR go-lives broke the feeds: one silent, one with blank chief complaints.

parts.label: What you reported
parts.criteria: The share computed over facilities with complete data, the same set as earlier weeks, with the gap stated; the facilities asked to fix and resend. Not the raw 3.4%, and not last week's counts copied in.
parts.modelAnswer: 6.4% from the two complete feeds, still rising, with a note and a revision promised.

parts.label: How you know
parts.criteria: The five-week trend on the same facilities, and their volumes against their averages.
parts.modelAnswer: 4.8 to 6.4% on Bayview and Hillcrest; volumes normal.

right.headline: Good: the feeds first, then the flu
right.body: A drop that starts the day two hospitals change EHRs is a data question. Completeness and field checks found one silent feed and one blank field; comparing the same facilities week to week showed ILI still rising.

gaps.headline: Sent, with gaps
gaps.body: The figure is right; it went late, or without the like-with-like trend to back it.

wrongSent.headline: A false decline reported
wrongSent.body: When the facility set or a key field changes, a share changes for reasons that are not epidemiology. Check completeness and fields before reading a trend.

fabricated.headline: Invented data
fabricated.body: Copying last week's counts makes the total look normal and the report untrue. State the gap; never fill it with numbers nobody observed.

notSent.headline: Nothing sent
notSent.body: Safe, but hospitals needed the figure, and a consistent-facility share was ready.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: Nothing was recorded before the case's limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Syndromic surveillance turns ED visits into near real-time signals, and its trends are only as good as the feeds behind them. A drop that begins the day two hospitals go live on new EHRs points to the data: Riverside's feed stopped and Northgate's chief complaints arrive empty, so the ILI share's numerator and denominator lost different things. Report the share over the facilities with complete feeds, the same set as earlier weeks, with the gap stated: 6.4% and still rising. Copying last week's counts invents data. Ask both facilities to fix their routing and mapping and resend the backlog.
